title: Exception Handling

sections.markdown: Exceptions are objects representing abnormal conditions. The hierarchy: Throwable → Error (fatal, don't catch) and Exception → RuntimeException (unchecked) vs checked exceptions.
Swallowing exceptions: `catch (Exception e) {}` hides bugs. Never catch-and-ignore; at minimum log with context, and never catch Throwable/Error.
Catch the most specific exception, fail fast, wrap-and-rethrow preserving the cause, and use try-with-resources for anything closeable. Throw early, catch late.

flashcards.back: Checked must be caught/declared (IOException); unchecked (RuntimeException) need not be — usually programming bugs.
Automatically closes resources implementing AutoCloseable, even on exception.
Error = serious, unrecoverable (OutOfMemory) — don't catch. Exception = conditions an app may handle.

quiz.explain: IOException is checked; the others are RuntimeExceptions (unchecked).

quiz.q: try-with-resources requires the resource to implement…

quiz.explain: Preserving the cause keeps the stack trace for debugging.

challenges.text: Create a custom checked exception and a custom unchecked exception.
Refactor manual close() in finally blocks to try-with-resources.
Implement a retry wrapper that retries on specific exceptions with backoff.
Demonstrate suppressed exceptions from try-with-resources and read them.
